# Helper functions

Here we show the functions being used to generate the supplementary material.
All of the following functions are compsed of R code and are used to generate the figures, tables, and statitics.

## Setup

```{r setup, echo=TRUE}
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(dplyr)
library(PupillometryR)


NAMES = c('compressed','aggregated','unaggregated')
SHAPE <- c(20,20,20)
cb_palette <- c('#D81B1B', '#FFDC07','#004D40')
data_dir <- '../../'
c_task_id_lists <- c(146818,359954,359955,190146,168757,359956,
                        359958,359959,2073,359960,168784,359962)

p_theme <- theme(
  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 17, hjust=0.5),
  panel.border = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  legend.title=element_text(size=17),
  legend.text=element_text(size=17),
  axis.title = element_text(size=17),
  axis.text = element_text(size=11),
  axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.5),
  legend.position="bottom",
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f1f2f5",
                                  colour = "white",
                                  size = 0.5, linetype = "solid"))

results <- read.csv("./k5_data.csv")
results$validation <- factor(results$validation, levels = NAMES)
seed_offset <- 100
```

## Test set plot
```{r test-plot, echo=TRUE}
test_plot <- function(data) { return(
    ggplot(data,
    aes(x = validation, y = testing_performance, color = validation,
                fill = validation, shape = validation)) +
    geom_flat_violin(position = position_nudge(x = 0.1, y = 0),
                    scale = "width", alpha = 0.2, width = 1.5) +
    geom_boxplot(color = "black", width = .08, outlier.shape = NA,
                alpha = 0.0, linewidth = 0.8,
                position = position_nudge(x = .15, y = 0)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.03,
                height = 0.0), size = 1.5, alpha = 1.0) +
    scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Accuracy %",
    labels = scales::percent,

    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
    name = "Validation"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = SHAPE,) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cb_palette,) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cb_palette,) +
    ggtitle('Accuracy on test set') +
    p_theme +
    guides(
    shape=guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
                        title = "Validation"),
    color=guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
                        title = "Validation"),
    fill=guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
                        title = "Validation")) +
    theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
            axis.text.x = element_blank(),
            axis.title.x = element_blank(),
            axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.5))
)}
```

## Test set results summary
```{r test-results-summary, echo=TRUE}
test_results_summary <- function(data) {
    return(
        data %>%
        group_by(validation) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(
            count = n(),
            na_cnt = sum(is.na(testing_performance)),
            min = min(testing_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(testing_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(testing_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(testing_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR = IQR(testing_performance, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
}
```

## Permutaiton test results
```{r test-results-stats, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
# permutation test with t-test statistic
# assuming we are using an alpha of 0.05
perm_test_maxt <- function(x, y, z, alternative = "two.sided", n_perm = 1000, seed = NULL,
                           x_name = NULL, y_name = NULL, z_name = NULL) {
  # Optionally set a seed for reproducibility
  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)

  # Combine the data and create a grouping factor.
  # Assuming each condition has the same sample size.
  n <- length(x)
  data_all <- c(x, y, z)
  groups <- factor(rep(c("X", "Y", "Z"), each = n))

  # Compute observed Welch t-tests for all pairwise comparisons.
  test_XY <- t.test(x, y, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)
  test_XZ <- t.test(x, z, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)
  test_YZ <- t.test(y, z, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)

  t_obs_XY <- as.numeric(test_XY$statistic)
  t_obs_XZ <- as.numeric(test_XZ$statistic)
  t_obs_YZ <- as.numeric(test_YZ$statistic)

  # Store the permutation distribution of the max (or min) t-statistics.
  max_stats_perm <- numeric(n_perm)

  for (i in 1:n_perm) {
    # Permute the group labels while preserving group sizes.
    permuted_labels <- sample(groups)

    # Create permuted groups based on the shuffled labels.
    x_perm <- data_all[permuted_labels == "X"]
    y_perm <- data_all[permuted_labels == "Y"]
    z_perm <- data_all[permuted_labels == "Z"]

    # Compute Welch t-tests on the permuted data.
    t_perm_XY <- tryCatch(t.test(x_perm, y_perm, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA)
    t_perm_XZ <- tryCatch(t.test(x_perm, z_perm, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA)
    t_perm_YZ <- tryCatch(t.test(y_perm, z_perm, alternative = alternative, var.equal = FALSE)$statistic, error = function(e) NA)

    # Adjust according to the type of test.
    if (alternative == "two.sided") {
      stats_perm <- abs(c(t_perm_XY, t_perm_XZ, t_perm_YZ))
      max_stats_perm[i] <- max(stats_perm, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else if (alternative == "greater") {
      stats_perm <- c(t_perm_XY, t_perm_XZ, t_perm_YZ)
      max_stats_perm[i] <- max(stats_perm, na.rm = TRUE)
    } else if (alternative == "less") {
      stats_perm <- c(t_perm_XY, t_perm_XZ, t_perm_YZ)
      max_stats_perm[i] <- min(stats_perm, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }

  # Compute adjusted p-values.
  # For two-sided: p = proportion of permuted max absolute t-statistics >= observed absolute t
  # For one-tailed "greater": p = proportion of permuted max t >= observed t
  # For one-tailed "less": p = proportion of permuted min t <= observed t; otherwise p = 1
  pval_XY <- pval_XZ <- pval_YZ <- NA

  if (alternative == "two.sided") {
    pval_XY <- mean(max_stats_perm >= abs(t_obs_XY))
    pval_XZ <- mean(max_stats_perm >= abs(t_obs_XZ))
    pval_YZ <- mean(max_stats_perm >= abs(t_obs_YZ))
  } else if (alternative == "greater") {
    pval_XY <- mean(max_stats_perm >= t_obs_XY)
    pval_XZ <- mean(max_stats_perm >= t_obs_XZ)
    pval_YZ <- mean(max_stats_perm >= t_obs_YZ)
  } else if (alternative == "less") {
    pval_XY <- mean(max_stats_perm <= t_obs_XY)
    pval_XZ <- mean(max_stats_perm <= t_obs_XZ)
    pval_YZ <- mean(max_stats_perm <= t_obs_YZ)
  }

  # check if pval are 0, if so set to 1/n_perm
  if (pval_XY == 0) pval_XY <- 1 / n_perm
  if (pval_XZ == 0) pval_XZ <- 1 / n_perm
  if (pval_YZ == 0) pval_YZ <- 1 / n_perm

  original <- c("X vs Y", "X vs Z", "Y vs Z")
  # Replace "X" with x_name if provided
  if (!is.null(x_name)) {
    original <- gsub("X", x_name, original)
  }

  # Replace "Y" with y_name if provided
  if (!is.null(y_name)) {
    original <- gsub("Y", y_name, original)
  }

  # Replace "Z" with z_name if provided
  if (!is.null(z_name)) {
    original <- gsub("Z", z_name, original)
  }

  # Create a results data frame.
  results <- data.frame(
    Comparison = original,
    Observed_t = c(t_obs_XY, t_obs_XZ, t_obs_YZ),
    Adjusted_p = c(pval_XY, pval_XZ, pval_YZ)
  )

  # Return the data frame.
  return(results)
}
```

## Selection set plot
```{r select-plot, echo=TRUE}
selection_plot <- function(data) { return(
    ggplot(data,
    aes(x = validation, y = training_performance, color = validation,
                fill = validation, shape = validation)) +
    geom_flat_violin(position = position_nudge(x = 0.1, y = 0),
                    scale = "width", alpha = 0.2, width = 1.5) +
    geom_boxplot(color = "black", width = .08, outlier.shape = NA,
                alpha = 0.0, linewidth = 0.8,
                position = position_nudge(x = .15, y = 0)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.03,
                height = 0.0), size = 1.5, alpha = 1.0) +
    scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Accuracy %",
    labels = scales::percent,

    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
    name = "Selection set"
    ) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = SHAPE,) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cb_palette,) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cb_palette,) +
    ggtitle('Accuracy on validation set') +
    p_theme +
    guides(
    shape=guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
                        title = "Validation"),
    color=guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
                        title = "Validation"),
    fill=guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "left",
                        title = "Validation")) +
    theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
            axis.text.x = element_blank(),
            axis.title.x = element_blank(),
            axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0.5))
)}
```

## Selection set results summary
```{r validation-results-summary, echo=TRUE}
selection_results_summary <- function(data) {
    return(
        data %>%
        group_by(validation) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(
            count = n(),
            na_cnt = sum(is.na(training_performance)),
            min = min(training_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(training_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean = mean(training_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(training_performance, na.rm = TRUE),
            IQR = IQR(training_performance, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
}
```
